content.title: Loan Officers
content.text: Video transcript available at https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Dm_6sQ_YTRU. Quick Facts: Loan Officers 2024 Median Pay $74,180 per year $35.66 per hour Typical Entry-Level Education Bachelor's degree Work Experience in a Related Occupation Less than 5 years On-the-job Training Moderate-term on-the-job training Number of Jobs, 2024 301,400 Job Outlook, 2024–34 2% (Slower than average) Employment Change, 2024–34 5,000 What Loan Officers Do Loan officers evaluate, authorize, or recommend approval of loan applications. Work Environment Most loan officers are employed by commercial banks, credit unions, mortgage companies, and other financial institutions. Most loan officers work full time, and some work more than 40 hours per week. Except for consumer loan officers, who spend most of their time in offices, these workers may travel to visit clients. How to Become a Loan Officer Loan officers typically need a bachelor’s degree and on-the-job training. Mortgage loan officers must be licensed. Pay The median annual wage for loan officers was $74,180 in May 2024. Job Outlook Employment of loan officers is projected to grow 2 percent from 2024 to 2034, slower than the average for all occupations. Despite limited employment growth, about 20,300 openings for loan officers are projected each year, on average, over the decade. Most of those openings are expected to result from the need to replace workers who transfer to different occupations or exit the labor force, such as to retire.
